questions.text:
Tiwai Point in the South Island of New Zealand extracts large amounts of aluminium sourced from an ore called bauxite, which contains the mineral aluminium(III) oxide, Al₂O₃. One step of the main extraction process is as follows:

Al₂O₃(s) + 2NaOH(aq) -> 2NaAlO₂(aq) + H₂O(l)

The graph below shows the mass of aluminium(III) oxide, Al₂O₃, as it reacts with 0.5 mol L⁻¹ NaOH. The graph has two sections: Section A (steep decline) and Section B (curve levelling off).

Add a second line to the graph to predict the rate of decline in mass of aluminium(III) oxide if 2 mol L⁻¹ NaOH were used in the reaction instead.

Assume both reactions started with the same mass of ore.
questions.expectedAnswer: Added line should have a steeper gradient, and begin and end at the same mass of Al₂O₃
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct second line (steeper gradient, same start and end mass).

questions.text:
With reference to the line you have drawn, explain the effect that this change in concentration of NaOH from 0.5 mol L⁻¹ to 2 mol L⁻¹ would have on the rate of this reaction.

In your answer you should include reference to:
- mass of Al₂O₃
- each section of the line
- collision theory.
questions.expectedAnswer: The added line shows a steeper decline in mass of Al₂O₃ due to the higher concentration of NaOH,
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States that the same mass of Al₂O₃ is used (starts or ends) OR correctly identifies that higher concentration increases rate of reaction. Merit: Correctly links increased concentration to the increase in frequency of successful collisions OR a correct comparison of sections A and B OR correctly identifies that the end point is reached sooner. Excellence: Full comparison including a correct comparison of sections A and B linked to the gradient of one line, which links the increase in concentration to the increase in frequency of successful collisions and an increase in the rate of reaction.

questions.text: For the 0.5 mol L⁻¹ NaOH solution, calculate the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺, concentration.
Calculate the pH of the 0.5 mol L⁻¹ NaOH solution.
questions.expectedAnswer:
pH = -log(2 x 10⁻¹⁴) = 13.7 (1 s.f.)
Accept use of pH = 14 - pOH.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Incorrectly calculates pH using [OH⁻]. Merit: Correct pH (sig figs are not required).

questions.text:
Using the principles of collision and particle theories, explain why using a catalyst would help to increase the rate of production of sodium aluminium salt (NaAlO₂).

You should include an energy profile diagram to support your answer.
questions.expectedAnswer: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by providing an alternative pathway for the reaction...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Basic definition of a catalyst (lowers activation energy and provides an alternative pathway). Merit: Links the higher rate of reaction to the lower activation energy requirement and the catalyst providing the alternative pathway. Excellence: Explanation including reference to activation energy, alternative pathway, successful collisions, and correct energy profile diagram.

questions.text:
Superphosphate fertiliser is manufactured in New Zealand using phosphorite rocks and sulfuric acid. The sulfuric acid is often produced on site, and includes a reaction involving oxygen, O₂(g), sulfur dioxide, SO₂(g), and sulfur trioxide, SO₃(g), which is represented by the equilibrium constant expression below.

Kc = [SO₃]² / ([SO₂]²[O₂])     Kc = 32.7 at 25 degrees C

Give the equation for this reaction.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct equation without states. Merit: First step correct but inverted answer. Excellence: Correct value including full working.

questions.text:
The reaction is set up and allowed to reach equilibrium.

Calculate the concentration of oxygen, O₂, at equilibrium if the concentration of sulfur dioxide, SO₂, is 0.17 mol L⁻¹ and sulfur trioxide, SO₃, is 0.50 mol L⁻¹.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct substitution but inverted value or not the same as Kc value calculated. Merit: Correct value (sig figs are not required). Excellence: Correct value including full working.

questions.text:
The reaction is set up differently, with concentrations of each component as indicated below.

[SO₃] = 0.530 mol L⁻¹
[O₂] = 0.710 mol L⁻¹
[SO₂] = 0.620 mol L⁻¹

Using a calculation, explain why this reaction is not at equilibrium.
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: States the calculated value is not the same as Kc value. Merit: States the value is less than Kc and therefore the reaction proceeds forwards (more products). Excellence: Identifies the reaction proceeds forwards with full explanation.

questions.text: Explain what must occur for the reaction to establish equilibrium.
questions.expectedAnswer: To establish equilibrium, the forward reaction must proceed at a greater rate than the reverse,
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correctly identifies direction based on answer from (b)(i). Merit: States the value is the same as Kc and therefore the reaction proceeds forwards. Excellence: Identifies the reaction proceeds forwards and explains in relation to products and reactants.

questions.text:
Sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄, can be manufactured using the following reaction:

SO₃(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ H₂SO₄(g)

Using equilibrium principles, identify, then describe, the effect on the position of the equilibrium when:

- water vapour, H₂O(g), is added to the reaction mixture.
Circle your choice: Forward is favoured / No Change / Reverse is favoured

- sodium hydroxide, NaOH(aq), is added to the reaction mixture.
Circle your choice: Forward is favoured / No Change / Reverse is favoured
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: One correct answer. Merit: Either correct answer linked to a reason for the shift and the outcome. Excellence: Justification of increase favouring forward reaction and products for either (c)(i) or (c)(ii).

questions.text:
This reaction can be performed under high pressure.

Explain why this is beneficial to the manufacturing process.
questions.expectedAnswer: Le Chatelier's principle states that increasing the pressure will favour the reaction that...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies it will favour products with no explanation. Merit: Explains increase favours side with fewer gas moles which favours the forward direction.

questions.text:
A reaction of HSO₄⁻ is shown below:

HSO₄⁻(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) ⇌ SO₄²⁻(aq) + HCO₃⁻(aq)

Identify the species acting as an acid and the species acting as a base in the above equation, and their conjugate pairs.

Acid:                Conjugate base:
Base:                Conjugate acid:
questions.expectedAnswer: Acid: HSO₄⁻, Conjugate base: SO₄²⁻. Base: CO₃²⁻, Conjugate acid: HCO₃⁻.

questions.text: Write the equilibrium constant expression, Kc, for this process.

This reaction was initially performed at 25 degrees C to determine the Kc value. When the reaction temperature was increased to 50 degrees C, the Kc value increased.

Explain whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic.
questions.expectedAnswer: Increasing the Kc value shows that the changes to the reaction has favoured the forward reaction
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Recognises that the forwards reaction is endothermic OR identifies that Kc increase shows products favoured. Merit: Explains that the Kc increase shows products were favoured when temperature is increased AND explains that increasing temperature favours the endothermic reaction to minimise the change. Excellence: Endothermic nature of the forwards reaction is justified linked to the increase in Kc due to temperature.

questions.text:
Solutions of 0.1 mol L⁻¹ concentration were made of each of the following three substances:

NH₃          HNO₃          NH₄Cl

Explain the pH of each of these solutions.

Include:
- a choice of pH value for each substance from the options below
- a classification for each substance
- any equations to explain the pH value.

pH options:    1-2    4-5    7    9-10    13-14
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Identifies 2 correct pH values OR correctly classifies substances. Merit: Correct statement about the concentration of species linked to pH OR correct equations for relevant substances. Excellence: Full justification including correct equations for all three species (does not need to include NH₄Cl pH if reasoning for other two is comprehensive).

questions.text:
Discuss the conductivity of the solutions:

NH₃          HNO₃          NH₄Cl

Note they are all equal in concentration.

In your answer you should:
- explain the requirements for a solution to conduct electricity
- compare the extent of conductivity of each substance
- reference the relevant equations from your previous answer to part (b)(i).
questions.expectedAnswer: HNO₃ is a strong acid, so it completely dissociates in water, producing a large number of freely...
questions.markingGuide: Achievement: Correct statement about the conductivity of free species. Merit: Correct statement of relative concentrations of species linked to conductivity. Excellence: Full justification including all three species (does not need exact ranking, but reasoning for each).
